rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening clause explains the preceding extraordinary honor; its nominal opening signals continuity, while its verbal predicate signals renewed prayer over time.
rows.anchor: الجملة تفيد الدوام نظرا إلى صدرها من حيث أنها جملة أسمية وتفيد التجدد نظرا إلى عجزها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic إن marks the importance of the statement, or answers the implicit question about the cause of this great honor.
rows.anchor: وتأكيدها بأن للإعتناء بشأن الخبر وقيل لوقوعها في جواب سؤال مقدر هو ما سبب هذا التشريف العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him the Prophet rather than naming him, contrary to the usual way God recounts His prophets, signals his exceptional dignity; the definite article marks him as the preeminent bearer of the title.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالنبي دون أسمه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على خلاف الغالب في حكايته تعالى عن أنبيائه

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: Some eminent scholars say النبي is used instead of الرسول to connect with the preceding رسول الله; since most hold messengership superior to prophethood, attaching prayer to the lower rank underscores his entitlement. Al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salam disagrees.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الأجلة : إن ذاك للأشعار بعلة الحكم ولم يعبر بالرسول بدله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annexation in ملائكته conveys comprehensiveness.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الملائكة للإستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying His angels highlights their rank; their attribution to God honors the Prophet, and the vast company conveys prayer reaching him continuously through the ages.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( ملائكته ) ولم يقل الملائكة إشارة إلى عظيم قدرهم ومزيد شرفهم بإضافتهم إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya explains God's prayer as His praise and exaltation of the Prophet before the angels; al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas also transmits this explanation, which al-Halimi adopts.
rows.anchor: هي منه عزوجل ثناؤه عليه عند ملائكته وتعظيمه ورواه البخاري عن أبي العالية وغيره عن الربيع بن أنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This exaltation appears in the world by raising his mention, manifesting his religion and preserving his law, and in the afterlife through intercession, reward, the Praised Station and precedence among the honored.
rows.anchor: تعظيمه تعالى إياه في الدنيا بإعلاء ذكره وإظهار دينه وإبقاء العمل بشريعته وفي الآخرة بتشفيعه في أمته

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: The angels' prayer means their supplication for the Prophet, according to Abu al-ʿAliya as transmitted by ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim.
rows.anchor: وهي من الملائكة الدعاء له عليه الصلاة والسلام على ما رواه عبد بن حميد وإبن أبي حاتم عن أبي العالية

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes God's prayer His mercy; al-Thawri and other scholars, Abu al-ʿAliya and al-Dahhak transmit it, and al-Mawardi calls it the most apparent explanation.
rows.anchor: هي منه تعالى رحمته عزوجل ونقله الترمذي عن الثوري وغير واحد من أهل العلم ونقل عن أبي العالية أيضا وعن الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection to understanding God's prayer as mercy refers back to the discussion of 33:43, هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته; the same answer applies.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ( هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ) والجواب هو الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions' question about how to pray for the Prophet suggests they distinguished prayer from ordinary mercy, since they already knew how to ask for mercy in the tashahhud.
rows.anchor: بأن الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم سألوا كما سيأتي قريبا إن شاء الله تعالى لما نزلت عن كيفية الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A response says the prayer is a particular mercy, so they asked how to obtain that specific kind; this makes the word carry two meanings for God and the angels, which many Hanafis and others reject.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنها رحمة خاصة فسألوا عن الكيفية ليحيطوا علما بذلك الخصوص وهي من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One solution to the two-meanings objection posits ellipsis: God prays and the angels pray, with a separate verb suited to each meaning.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : في الآية حذف والأصل إن الله يصلي وملائكته يصلون فيكون قد أدى كل معنى بلفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reply is that having multiple agents makes the verb function as though it were multiple verbs.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر : تعدد الفاعل صير الفعل كالمتعدد

rows.speaker: صدر الشريعة
rows.claim: Sadr al-Shariʿa proposes one literal meaning, supplication for good: God directs Himself and the angels to convey good, which means mercy for God and seeking forgiveness for angels; al-Alusi finds this doubtful.
rows.anchor: وقال صدر الشريعة يجوز أن يكون المعنى واحدا حقيقا وهو الدعاء والمعنى والله تعالى أعلم أنه تعالى يدعو ذاته

rows.speaker: جمع من المحققين
rows.claim: A group of careful scholars avoids equivocation through a general metaphor: care for the Prophet's good and welfare, disclosure of his honor and magnification, or spiritual compassion.
rows.anchor: وقال جمع من المحققين : يتقصى عن ذلك بعموم المجاز فيراد معنى مجازي عام يكون كل من المعاني فردا حقيقيا له

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: Some eminent scholars say the meaning of prayer changes according to the state of the one praying, the recipient of prayer, and the one prayed for.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الأجلة : إن معنى الصلاة يختلف بإعتبار حال المصلي والمصلي له والمصلي عليه

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: Another view says prayer has one linguistic sense, inclination or favor (عطف): mercy for God, seeking forgiveness for angels, and supplication for people; critics object that literal inclination cannot be predicated of God, while its defenders distinguish unseen divine reality from bodily human experience.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر : الصواب أن الصلاة لغة بمعنى واحد وهو العطف ثم هو بالنسبة إليه تعالى الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Salaf did not reinterpret divine mercy through the two familiar figurative explanations; requiring such interpretation would leave very little scripture without it.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب السلف إلى عدم تأويل الرحمة فيه تعالى بأحد التأويلين المشهورين مع أنها في الشاهد لا تتحقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi favors prayer here as honoring the Prophet, with an inclination appropriate to God and the angels; when applied to believers, it means what suits each of them.
rows.anchor: وقد يختار أن الصلاة هنا تعظيم لشأنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقارنه عطف لائق به تعالى وبملائكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining God and angels under one pronoun can honor the angels without implying any deficiency in God.
rows.anchor: وجمع الله سبحانه والملائكة في ضمير واحد لا ينافي قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام لمن قال

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet rebuked a preacher who said whoever obeys God and His Messenger has prospered and whoever disobeys them has strayed, telling him to repeat Allah and His Messenger separately.
rows.anchor: بئس خطيب القوم أنت قل ومن يعص الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say combining the two is generally unobjectionable; the preacher was censured for pausing after يعصهما, and they cite a report in Abu Dawud.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا بأس بذلك مطلقا وذم الخطيب لأنه وقف على يعصهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view calls the combined pronoun objectionable across two clauses but acceptable in one clause, as here and in the Prophet's speech; al-Alusi says this needs examination.
rows.anchor: وقيل يقبح إذا كان في جملتين كما في كلام الخطيب ولا يقبح إذا كان في واحدة كما في الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعبدالوارث عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAbd al-Warith from Abu ʿAmr read ملائكته in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبن عباس وعبدالوارث عن أبي عمرو ( وملائكته ) بالرفع

rows.speaker: الكوفيون غير الفراء
rows.claim: The Kufans other than al-Farraʾ construe the nominative as coordinated with the syntactic position of إن and its subject.
rows.anchor: فعند الكوفيين غير الفراء هو عطف على محل أن وأسمها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ permits coordination with إن's subject when its case ending is hidden, as in 2:62 and the cited verse of poetry; grammarians differ whether this covers a noun ending in a long vowel or one annexed to ياء.
rows.anchor: والفراء يشترط في العطف على ذلك خفاء إعراب أسم إن كما في قوله تعالى ( إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون )

rows.speaker: البصريون والفراء
rows.claim: The Basrans and al-Farraʾ instead parse ملائكته as a subject whose predicate is يصلون, with إن's predicate omitted because the following clause makes it clear: God prays and His angels pray.
rows.anchor: وعند البصريين والفراء هو مبتدأ وجملة ( يصلون ) خبره وخبر إن محذوف ثقة بدلالة ما بعد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command calls believers to honor the Prophet in keeping with the honor God and the angels give him; its surface wording does not explicitly command imitation.
rows.anchor: أي عظموا شأنه عاطفين عليه فإنكم أولى بذلك وظاهر سوق الآية أنه لا يجاب إقتدائنا به تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud's reading صلوا عليه كما صلى عليه and al-Hasan's فصلوا عليه make the preceding interpretation clearer and weaken the claim that the command means simply to say a fixed invocation.
rows.anchor: قراءة إبن مسعود صلوا عليه كما صلى عليه وكذا قراءة الحسن فصلوا عليه أظهر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Those who gloss the command as saying اللهم صل على النبي mean that this wording, or a similar invocation asking God to honor him, is the commanded form because believers cannot fulfill his due honor themselves.
rows.anchor: ومن فسره بذلك أراد أن المراد بالتعظيم المأمور به ما يكون بهذا اللفظ ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted formulas guide believers to the manner and form of prayer; they do not define the lexical meaning of صلوا, and their several forms may be combined.
rows.anchor: وما جاء في الأخبار إرشاد إلى كيفية ذلك وصفته لا أنه تفسير للفظ صلوا وجاء ذلك على عدة أوجه

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra reports that a man asked how to pray for the Prophet after learning the greeting; the Prophet taught asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham's family, and to bless them. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : قال رجل : يارسول الله أما السلام عليك فقد علمناه

rows.speaker: أبو حميد الساعدي
rows.claim: Abu Humayd al-Saʿidi reports that the Prophet taught praying for Muhammad, his wives and descendants as for Abraham's family, and asking blessing for them likewise. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حميد الساعدي أنهم قالوا : يارسول الله كيف نصلي عليك فقال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports that the Prophet taught asking God to pray upon His servant and messenger as upon Abraham and to bless Muhammad and his family as Abraham. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قلنا : يارسول الله هذا السلام عليك قد علمنا فكيف الصلاة عليك

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet taught asking God to pray upon and bless Muhammad and his family as He did Abraham and his family throughout the worlds, ending with حميد مجيد; the greeting was already known. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة إنهم سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف نصلي عليك قال : قولوا اللهم صل على محمد

rows.speaker: ابن بريدة
rows.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that the Prophet taught asking God to place His prayers, mercy and blessings upon Muhammad and his family as He placed them upon Abraham. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن إبن بريدة رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : قلنا يارسول الله قد علمنا كيف نسلم عليك فكيف نصلي عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi notes that some of the cited reports have been criticized, without specifying which ones here.
rows.anchor: إلى غير ذلك مما ملئت منه كتب الحديث إلا أن في بعض الروايات المذكورة فيها مقالا

rows.speaker: الباجي
rows.claim: The apparent question asks for the form or manner of prayer, as al-Baji prefers and al-Qurtubi states definitively; an alternative says they asked its meaning and wording because they expected a fixed liturgical formula and sought textual instruction rather than analogy.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من السؤال أنه سؤال عن الصفة كما أشرنا إليه قبل وهو الذي رجحه الباجي وغيره وجزم به القرطبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi favors the manner-of-prayer reading: after learning of God's and the angels' honoring, the Companions did not know which form of honor suited them, so the Prophet directed them to its best form and to ask God for it.
rows.anchor: لما سمعوا الأمر بالصلاة بعد سماع أن الله عزوجل وملائكته عليهم السلام يصلون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking God to pray upon the Prophet is the greatest form of honor because it acknowledges believers' inability to give him the honor he deserves.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يعلم أن الآتي بما أمر به من طلب الصلاة له صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عزوجل آت بأعظم أنواع التعظيم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: The saying attributed to Abu Bakr, the Siddiq, that inability to comprehend comprehension is itself comprehension roughly parallels this point.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل ونسب إلى الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه العجز عن درك الأدراك إدراك

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: A view transmitted and approved by Abu al-Yumn ibn ʿAsakir says believers delegate the prayer to God because He knows its due form and His intention; al-Alusi says his own formulation is subtler.
rows.anchor: قول بعض الأجلة ونقله أبو اليمن بن عساكر وحسنه لما أمرنا الله تعالى بالصلاة على نبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent direction of the Prophet's instruction requires asking God to pray for him; اللهم صل على محمد suffices because all the reported forms agree on it.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يحصل إمتثال الأمر إلا بما فيه طلب ذلك منه عزوجل ويكفي اللهم صل على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among those who require prayer upon the Prophet within ritual prayer, the stronger view accepts صلى الله على محمد, while الصلاة على رسول الله does not suffice by agreement because it does not attribute the prayer to God.
rows.anchor: يكفي صلى الله على محمد على الأصح بخلاف الصلاة على رسول الله فإنه لا يجزي إتفاقا

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar's Tuhfa says الصلاة على محمد apparently suffices if intended as supplication.
rows.anchor: وفي تحفة إبن حجر يكفي الصلاة على محمد إن نوى بها الدعاء فيما يظهر

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nishaburi says صليت على محمد is insufficient: the servant should ask his Lord to pray for the Prophet, so God is the actual agent and the servant is only figuratively praying.
rows.anchor: وقال النيسابوري : لا يكفي صليت على محمد لأن مرتبة العبد تقصر عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request form is considered better than the declarative form. The suggestion that hadith scholars use declaratives to avoid confusing lay listeners about whether God's prayer has occurred is weak; Al-Alusi prefers avoiding interruption and mixed styles in flowing prose.
rows.anchor: وذكروا أن الإتيان بصيغة الطلب أفضل من الإتيان بصيغة الخبر وأجيب عن إطباق المحدثين على الإتيان بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is not fulfilled by asking God merely to exalt Muhammad in suitably honoring terms without a word derived from prayer; the majority understand both commands as prescribed formulas, including اللهم صل على النبي and السلام عليك أيها النبي.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه لا يحصل الإمتثال باللهم عظم محمدا التعظيم اللائق ونحوه مما ليس فيه مشتق من الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first and strongest reading of السلام عليك is a prayer for the Prophet's safety from defects and harms, with السلام as a verbal noun meaning safety; على is used for praise rather than a sense of decree or dominion.
rows.anchor: والأرجح عندي هو الوجه الأول وقيل : معنى ( سلموا تسليما )

rows.speaker: ابن فورك
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes السلام as God's name and the phrase as His ongoing care and guardianship; Ibn Furak and others define the name as the possessor of safety from every defect in essence, attribute and act.
rows.anchor: ويكون السلام هنا أسم الله تعالى ومعناه على ما أختاره إبن فورك وغيره من عدة أقوال ذو السلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the divine-name reading, another explanation means that the Prophet be granted goodness and blessing and protected from harm, since invoking God's name upon something confers that benefit.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إذا أريد بالسلام ما هو من أسمائه تعالى فالمراد لا خلوت من الخير والبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation supplies an omitted word: حفظ الله عليك, a prayer that God preserve the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الكلام على هذا التقدير على حذف المضاف أي حفظ الله تعالى عليك والمراد الدعاء بالحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes salām as peace or non-opposition and asks God to make people submit to the Prophet and his law; على suits the turning toward someone in obedience.
rows.anchor: وثالثها الإنقياد عليك على أن السلام من المسالمة وعدم المخالفة والمراد الدعاء بأن يصير الله تعالى العباد منقادين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the command may mean obedience to the Prophet's orders, but the apparent reports and traditions support the greeting or prayer for safety, which most scholars adopt.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معنى ( سلموا تسليما ) إنقادوا لأوامره صلى الله عليه وسلم إنقيادا وهو غير بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is declarative in form but functions as a supplication asking God to grant the Prophet safety.
rows.anchor: والجملة صيغة خبر معناها الدعاء بالسلامة وطلبها منه تعالى لنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some raise a theological problem: supplication entails distinct requester, requested object and recipient; if God asks another for the Prophet's safety it is impossible, while asking Himself seems to require self-distinction.
rows.anchor: وأستشكل ذلك فيما إذا قال الله تعالى السلام عليك أيها النبي أو نحوه بأن الدعاء لا يتصور منه عزوجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply says one may request or will something of oneself just as one may will it of another; humans command and prohibit themselves, as scripture states, and God's request can more clearly be understood as His will.
rows.anchor: قال سبحانه ( إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explanations of اللهم سلم على النبي include: God, say peace upon him; God, bring or realize safety for him; and God, protect him from defects and harm.
rows.anchor: ومعنى اللهم سلم على النبي اللهم قل السلام على النبي

rows.speaker: بعض المعاصرين
rows.claim: A contemporary scholar treats God's السلام عليك as performative speech that creates safety, by analogy with contract formulas; Al-Alusi prefers the direct sense of bringing safety rather than saying the greeting, to reduce mediation.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المعاصرين : إن السلام عليك ونحوه من الله عزوجل لإنشاء السلامة وإيجادها بهذا اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's greeting of prophets means He has made them recipients of invocation and praise, as in His greetings to Noah, Abraham, Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون السلام منه عزوجل على أنبيائه عليهم السلام نحو قوله سبحانه ( سلام على نوح في العالمين سلام على إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تسليما is an emphatic verbal noun; salām is explicitly emphasized because God's and the angels' prayer already assures the prayer, whereas salām has no such confirming context.
rows.anchor: ونصب ( تسليما ) على أنه مصدر مؤكد وأكد سبحانه التسليم ولم يؤكد الصلاة قيل لأنها مؤكدة بإعلامه تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim explains that prayer is already emphatic through إن and the universal جمع for angels, urging immediate imitation; salām lacks that emphasis, so its verbal noun reinforces the bare command. Both prayers and greetings are repeated as report and request, and salām's later position makes emphasis useful.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا يؤل قول إبن القيم التأكيد فيهما وإن أختلف جهته فإنه تعالى أخبر في الأول بصلاته وصلاة ملائكته عليه مؤكدا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ellipsis analysis reconstructs صلوا عليه تصلية وسلموا عليه تسليما, omitting عليه from one clause and the verbal noun from the other; prayer is attributed to God and angels while believers are ordered to do both.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن في الكلام الإحتباك والأصل صلوا عليه تصلية وسلموا عليه تسليما فحذف عليه من إحدى الجملتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says God's and the angels' prayer includes greeting, while believers must also obey and submit; because their prayer need not include submission, they are explicitly commanded to greet and obey.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الصلاة من الله سبحانه والملائكة متضمنة للسلام بمعنى التحية الذي لا يتصور غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds the second explanation stronger: prayer by God and angels entails greeting, but believers must explicitly be told to submit, since their prayer does not entail both senses; he notes a difficulty in its argument.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل : وهذا أولى مما قبله لأن ذلك يرد عليه قوله تعالى : ( سلام على إبراهيم والملائكة يدخلون عليهم

rows.speaker: الشهاب الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Shihab al-Khafaji sees a subtle reason for the omission of divine and angelic salām and its emphasis for believers: the preceding passage discusses harm to the Prophet, which people inflict, and salām asks that he be kept safe from it.
rows.anchor: وقال الشهاب الخفاجي عليه الرحمة : قد لاح لي في ترك تأكيد السلام وتخصيصه بالمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tentative explanation says the believers already knew God's and the angels' greeting and the form of their own greeting; the verse's prayer statement could otherwise imply that salām was unimportant or its request abrogated, so it is commanded emphatically.
rows.anchor: وربما يقال على بعد في ذلك : إنه يمكن أن يكون سلام الله تعالى وملائكته عليه عليه الصلاة والسلام معلوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars treat the imperative as obligatory; some claim consensus. Al-Tabari's claim that it is recommended by consensus is rejected or construed as recommending more than the once-in-a-lifetime minimum, which al-Qurtubi says is undisputed.
rows.anchor: والأمر في الآية عند الأكثرين للوجوب بل ذكر بعضهم إجماع الأئمة والعلماء عليه ودعوى محمد بن جرير الطبري أنه للندب بالإجماع مردودة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومالك
rows.claim: The majority, including Abu Hanifa and Malik, require prayer once in a lifetime: the unrestricted command does not require repetition, and one performance fulfills the act.
rows.anchor: قيل : واجبة مرة في العمر ككلمة التوحيد لأن الأمر مطلق لا يقتضي تكرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other legal positions require prayer in every tashahhud or in every ritual prayer; a minority of Hanbalis make it a designated opening invocation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : واجبة في التشهد مطلقا وقيل : واجبة في مصلق الصلاة وتفرد بعض الحنابلة بتعين دعاء الإفتتاح بها

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن بكير
rows.claim: A position attributed to Qadi Abu Bakr ibn Bukayr requires frequent prayer without setting a number.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يجب الإكثار منها من غير تعيين بعدد وحكى ذلك عن القاضي أبي بكر بن بكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other positions require prayer once at each gathering, in every supplication, or each time the Prophet is mentioned.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تجب في كل مجلس مرة وإن تكرر ذكره صلى الله عليه وسلم مرارا

rows.speaker: الطحاوي
rows.claim: The view requiring prayer at every mention is held by groups of Hanafis, Shafiʿis, Malikis and some Hanbalis; al-Tahawi says it is due whenever one hears the Prophet mentioned or mentions him oneself.
rows.anchor: وبه قال جمع من الحنفية منهم الطحاوي وعبارته تجب كلما سمع ذكره من غيره أو ذكره بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proponents cite reports threatening humiliation, distance, misery, miserliness and rudeness for neglecting prayer; most regard these threats as signs of obligation, though the view was also linked to the weak rule that unrestricted commands imply repetition.
rows.anchor: قيل وهو مبني على القول الضعيف في الأصول أن الأمر المطلق يفيد التكرار وليس كذلك بل له أدلة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics say the every-mention duty contradicts prior consensus, since no Companion or Successor is known to have held it.
rows.anchor: وأعترض هذا القول كثيرون بأنه مخالف للأجماع المنعقد قبل قائله إذ لم يعرف عن صحابي ولا تابعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics argue the rule would prevent other worship and burden callers to prayer, listeners, reciters passing over the Prophet's name, and those uttering the two testimonies, contrary to the law's ease.
rows.anchor: وبأنه يلزم على عمومه أن لا يتفرغ السامع لعبادة أخرى وأنها تجب على المؤذن وسامعه والقاريء المار بذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics add that praising God whenever He is mentioned would be more deserving of obligation, yet proponents do not require it.
rows.anchor: وبأن الثناء على الله تعالى كلما ذكر أحق بالوجوب ولم يقولوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics note that no report preserves a Companion saying to the Prophet, may God pray upon you.
rows.anchor: وبأنه لا يحفظ عن صحابي أنه قال : يارسول الله صلى الله عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics answer that the warning reports are rhetorical exaggeration emphasizing the duty's importance, particularly for someone habitually neglecting prayer.
rows.anchor: وبأن تلك الأحاديث المحتج بها للوجوب خرجت مخرج المبالغة في تأكد ذلك وطلبه
